The second age of Ge'or began with the first permanent settlements — and with the first wars between species.

The demons were the most aggressive people of the age. Their warrior nature — raw, untamed, unrefined by the honor codes that would come later — drove their tribes to expand rapidly, taking territory by force. They earned enmity across the world: a reputation for violence that would follow them for millennia. Not because demons were evil. Because they were strong — and in a tribal world, strength means conquest. The seeds of the demon stigma were planted here, in the blood of the first tribal wars.

But the world was healing. The apocalyptic aftermath of the crash — the acid rains, the nuclear winter, the poisoned water — finally began to subside. The skies cleared. The climate stabilized. Crops could be grown reliably for the first time in generations. Populations surged. Tribes that had spent centuries just surviving began to thrive — building the first permanent villages, the first trade routes, the first alliances and the first grudges.

By nine thousand BGD, the tribes of Ge'or had grown large and organized enough to attempt something the world had never seen.

Civilization.
